criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use an oblique isometric projection with vertical structures and diagonal ground axes.
Both frame industrial generation opposite a larger urban load area.
different: REFERENCE is framed slightly tighter and lower around the central grid chain.
CANDIDATE is slightly wider and more top-down, exposing more empty central terrain.

evidence.observation: Tight isometric view centers the pylon chain between left industry and right city.
Comparable isometric yaw and pitch, but broader terrain and smaller distributed landmarks are visible.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both maps contain industrial clusters, utility corridors, and dense residential districts.
Both place the strongest urban mass toward the right or lower-right.
different: REFERENCE maintains nearly continuous roads, buildings, and terrain detail across the map.
CANDIDATE has broad sparse central fields and more isolated building clusters.

evidence.observation: Industrial, road, pylon, and housing detail occupies almost the entire visible world.
Dense edge districts surround a substantially emptier central map area.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use a winding dark channel to separate industrial and urban areas.
Both channels are embedded into the terrain rather than shown as bright blue water.
different: REFERENCE shows a broad, deep rocky ravine with pronounced banks and a diagonal course.
CANDIDATE shows a narrower, flatter outlined channel with weaker bank depth and unclear crossings.

evidence.observation: A wide shadowed ravine curves diagonally toward the lower-left with layered rocky banks.
A thin dark channel bends down the center-left with shallow, low-contrast banks.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Plants remain the largest industrial silhouettes, pylons occupy the middle tier, and homes remain smallest.
Substations are visually distinct from both towers and major facilities.
different: CANDIDATE civic and commercial blocks are chunkier relative to nearby pylons and substations.
REFERENCE has more varied plant and facility silhouette sizes.

evidence.observation: Large multi-part plants, medium pylons and substations, and small surrounding structures form a clear hierarchy.
The same broad hierarchy is present, though major blocks and utility sprites are more uniformly chunky.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use blackened industrial metal, brown soil, amber illumination, and cool cyan energy accents.
Both combine dark chrome HUD frames with a heat-washed world palette.
different: REFERENCE has richer rocky relief, concrete variation, highlights, and midtone separation.
CANDIDATE is darker and flatter, with repeated ground tiles and less surface cohesion.

evidence.observation: Layered rock, roads, roofs, metal, and localized amber lights create a strongly dimensional surface.
Matching sepia-black materials are visible, but terrain and structures have flatter tonal modeling.

criteria.label: RELATED
similar: Both use cyan conductors to connect pylons, substations, plants, and load areas.
Both introduce contrasting amber, yellow, or red routes for non-normal grid states.
different: REFERENCE routes form a compact, bright chain with clear tower attachment and one readable stressed segment.
CANDIDATE routes use many sweeping double lines and crossings, weakening endpoint and energized-path readability.

evidence.observation: Bright cyan-white links visibly terminate at successive towers and substations; an amber segment isolates stress.
Cyan arcs, a yellow dashed route, and a red dashed fault are distinct, but several routes overlap or sweep past nodes.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use segmented industrial chrome across the top, a vertical build kit on the left, and an inspector on the right.
Cyan, amber, and red status colors are integrated consistently with the map.
different: REFERENCE presents fewer, larger status readouts with stronger immediate hierarchy.
CANDIDATE panels are more text-dense, and several inspector and kit labels are visibly smaller.

evidence.observation: Large riveted top modules separate heat, supply, reserve, day, and pause status.
Right inspector uses a large asset image, capacity readout, unavailable state, and condition bar.
A closely matching riveted top bar separates settings, money, supply, heat alert, speed, and purchase.

criteria.label: PARITY
similar: Both explicitly show a +8°C heat event with a large pale sun and an amber-brown world wash.
Both pair the heat state with stressed or unavailable grid feedback.
different: REFERENCE emphasizes low reserve and an unavailable tower, while CANDIDATE emphasizes safety-boundary progress and a protected fault.

evidence.observation: The top HUD visibly combines HEAT +8°C, high demand, and 6% reserve.
Bright sun, warning context, and an unavailable 0 MW inspector reinforce the heat emergency.
The top alert visibly states a +8°C heatwave and morning safety-boundary status.

criteria.label: CLOSE
similar: Both use a centered four-cell black-metal strip occupying roughly one-third of the screen width.
Both clearly highlight the current cell in cyan and retain readable neighboring states.
different: REFERENCE uses a taller playback strip with large transport icons and speed labels.
CANDIDATE uses a thinner event-stage bar with smaller labels, completion checks, a current diamond, and pending rings.

evidence.observation: Four large chrome playback cells are centered at the bottom, with the active x1 cell outlined cyan.
An independent four-stage event bar shows completed, current, result, and next states with distinct progress glyphs.
